Reasoning: medium
Read pages for a research assistant. Preserve this source's evidence and follow
useful page links to fill missing fields. You do not decide the final answer.

Extraction and navigation are separate. During extraction, only the supplied page
is evidence. The original question specifies the fields to look for; it does not
establish facts. During navigation, parent notes and earlier reasoning can guide
link selection, but must not be copied into the current page's evidence.

Extract what this page can establish even if it cannot answer the whole question.
Preserve exact names, titles, dates, values, units and relevant lists. For tables,
keep each value attached to its entity and header, including year, variant and
population. Distinguish different measurements and totals from subgroups. Quote
short supporting text. Report missing fields as unknown. If the supplied page is
truncated, do not claim its unseen rows or candidates are absent. Describe list
coverage and date range so partial evidence cannot be mistaken for a complete set.

The current-page note is saved before navigation. Follow a page link when its label,
surrounding text or an observed same-site URL pattern suggests it can fill a
specific missing field. State that field and why the next page should supply it.
A relevant index may contain useful links without answer facts. A wrong-year page
can help if it links to the required year. Generic footer links on unrelated pages,
missing pages and repeated content do not justify expansion. After an unhelpful
child, choose a different supported route or stop. You may follow links outside
the menu and infer another address within a site already being read.

Child notes are preserved separately and returned automatically. Never rewrite
them as your own evidence. Keep useful Next links in your note even if the local
expansion budget is exhausted; unvisited links are not disqualified candidates.

For extraction return plain text/Markdown in this format:
**Final Information**
**Page:** Actual title and original URL.
**Evidence:** Relevant facts, lists or rows with exact fields and short source quotes.
**Coverage:** Which entities, years and conditions this page actually covers;
whether the supplied evidence is a full list, a subset, or a truncated excerpt.
**Missing:** Requested fields not established by this page.
**Next links:** Useful source URLs and the missing field each could establish.
**Expand:** yes or no, with a concrete reason.
**Status:** partial

Use answered only if this page supplies all requested facts; partial for useful

Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

How provisional and final data are used by various Data Tools

![Image 5](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

| Data Tool | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Data Trends (Trend Generator) | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used where both are available |
| Survey Data Complete Data Files | Provisional and final data files are included in the zip files for years where both provisional and final have been released. |
| Survey Data ACCESS Data Base | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final released data are used when both are available. Historical provisional data bases are not available. |
| Survey Data Custom Data Files Compare Institutions Statistical Tables Summary Tables | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used when available, but users are given the option to use provisional data. |
| Data Feedback Report | Data feedback reports are only created when data are provisionally released. Historic reports are available but are not recreated using final/revised data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Institution Profile) | Profiles are only based on the most current provisionally released data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Reported Data) | Historically the reported data tool contained only provisionally released data. Final data have recently been loaded for IPEDS collection years 2014-15 through 2021-22. |

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Provisional release data are used for First Look web tables. Final release data include revisions to the provisional release data that have been made by institutions during the subsequent data collection year. While the final release data offer the most up to date data, these data may not match tables from the First Look web tables based on provisional release data.

Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

How provisional and final data are used by various Data Tools

![Image 5](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

| Data Tool | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Data Trends (Trend Generator) | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used where both are available |
| Survey Data Complete Data Files | Provisional and final data files are included in the zip files for years where both provisional and final have been released. |
| Survey Data ACCESS Data Base | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final released data are used when both are available. Historical provisional data bases are not available. |
| Survey Data Custom Data Files Compare Institutions Statistical Tables Summary Tables | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used when available, but users are given the option to use provisional data. |
| Data Feedback Report | Data feedback reports are only created when data are provisionally released. Historic reports are available but are not recreated using final/revised data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Institution Profile) | Profiles are only based on the most current provisionally released data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Reported Data) | Historically the reported data tool contained only provisionally released data. Final data have recently been loaded for IPEDS collection years 2014-15 through 2021-22. |

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Provisional release data are used for First Look web tables. Final release data include revisions to the provisional release data that have been made by institutions during the subsequent data collection year. While the final release data offer the most up to date data, these data may not match tables from the First Look web tables based on provisional release data.

Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

![Image 5](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

| Data Tool | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Data Trends (Trend Generator) | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used where both are available |
| Survey Data Complete Data Files | Provisional and final data files are included in the zip files for years where both provisional and final have been released. |
| Survey Data ACCESS Data Base | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final released data are used when both are available. Historical provisional data bases are not available. |
| Survey Data Custom Data Files Compare Institutions Statistical Tables Summary Tables | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used when available, but users are given the option to use provisional data. |
| Data Feedback Report | Data feedback reports are only created when data are provisionally released. Historic reports are available but are not recreated using final/revised data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Institution Profile) | Profiles are only based on the most current provisionally released data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Reported Data) | Historically the reported data tool contained only provisionally released data. Final data have recently been loaded for IPEDS collection years 2014-15 through 2021-22. |

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Provisional release data are used for First Look web tables. Final release data include revisions to the provisional release data that have been made by institutions during the subsequent data collection year. While the final release data offer the most up to date data, these data may not match tables from the First Look web tables based on provisional release data.

Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

How provisional and final data are used by various Data Tools

![Image 5](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

| Data Tool | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Data Trends (Trend Generator) | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used where both are available |
| Survey Data Complete Data Files | Provisional and final data files are included in the zip files for years where both provisional and final have been released. |
| Survey Data ACCESS Data Base | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final released data are used when both are available. Historical provisional data bases are not available. |
| Survey Data Custom Data Files Compare Institutions Statistical Tables Summary Tables | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used when available, but users are given the option to use provisional data. |
| Data Feedback Report | Data feedback reports are only created when data are provisionally released. Historic reports are available but are not recreated using final/revised data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Institution Profile) | Profiles are only based on the most current provisionally released data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Reported Data) | Historically the reported data tool contained only provisionally released data. Final data have recently been loaded for IPEDS collection years 2014-15 through 2021-22. |

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Provisional release data are used for First Look web tables. Final release data include revisions to the provisional release data that have been made by institutions during the subsequent data collection year. While the final release data offer the most up to date data, these data may not match tables from the First Look web tables based on provisional release data.

Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

How provisional and final data are used by various Data Tools

![Image 5](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

| Data Tool | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Data Trends (Trend Generator) | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used where both are available |
| Survey Data Complete Data Files | Provisional and final data files are included in the zip files for years where both provisional and final have been released. |
| Survey Data ACCESS Data Base | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final released data are used when both are available. Historical provisional data bases are not available. |
| Survey Data Custom Data Files Compare Institutions Statistical Tables Summary Tables | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used when available, but users are given the option to use provisional data. |
| Data Feedback Report | Data feedback reports are only created when data are provisionally released. Historic reports are available but are not recreated using final/revised data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Institution Profile) | Profiles are only based on the most current provisionally released data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Reported Data) | Historically the reported data tool contained only provisionally released data. Final data have recently been loaded for IPEDS collection years 2014-15 through 2021-22. |

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Provisional release data are used for First Look web tables. Final release data include revisions to the provisional release data that have been made by institutions during the subsequent data collection year. While the final release data offer the most up to date data, these data may not match tables from the First Look web tables based on provisional release data.

Timing of IPEDS Provisional and Final Data Releases

![Image 4](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

Quality control procedures and institution follow-up continue two to three months after a collection period closes. Missing data are imputed due to nonresponse to entire survey components or items. The provisional release of the edited and imputed data will include a set of WEB tables that formerly appeared in IPEDS First Look reports as well as a Data Release Memo that summarizes response rate information for each survey. The final data release is available after institutions have had a chance to revise their data in the following year. Final data are not issued with a set of WEB tables and a Data Release Memo.

The timing of the releases can vary somewhat depending on the nature of the internal process, but generally will follow this timetable:

| Collection Period | Survey Components | Collection closes | Provisional data | Final (Revised) data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FALL | IC, C, E12 | November | Approximately 7 months after collection closes | Approximately 7 months after institutions have revised their data the following year |
| WINTER | ADM, GR, SFA, OM | March |
| SPRING | EF, F, HR, AL | April |
| _WEB Tables and Data Release Memo_ | Yes | No |

The current review process for the data releases began with the 2018-19 IPEDS survey year and continues to undergo improvements. However, approval of the data release is subject to multiple steps in the review process and unanticipated delays can occur. The goal of NCES is to maintain or improve the timeliness of data release on an annual basis.

How provisional and final data are used by various Data Tools

![Image 5](https://nces.ed.gov/ipeds/datacenter/images/icon_close.svg)

| Data Tool | Usage |
| --- | --- |
| Data Trends (Trend Generator) | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used where both are available |
| Survey Data Complete Data Files | Provisional and final data files are included in the zip files for years where both provisional and final have been released. |
| Survey Data ACCESS Data Base | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final released data are used when both are available. Historical provisional data bases are not available. |
| Survey Data Custom Data Files Compare Institutions Statistical Tables Summary Tables | Provisional released data are used for the current year. Final data are used when available, but users are given the option to use provisional data. |
| Data Feedback Report | Data feedback reports are only created when data are provisionally released. Historic reports are available but are not recreated using final/revised data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Institution Profile) | Profiles are only based on the most current provisionally released data. |
| Look Up an Institution (Reported Data) | Historically the reported data tool contained only provisionally released data. Final data have recently been loaded for IPEDS collection years 2014-15 through 2021-22. |

IPEDS data, including provisional release data and final release data, adhere to rigorous quality control procedures established by NCES. Data are imputed for nonresponding institutions. Provisional release data are used for First Look web tables. Final release data include revisions to the provisional release data that have been made by institutions during the subsequent data collection year. While the final release data offer the most up to date data, these data may not match tables from the First Look web tables based on provisional release data.

**Wyoming** ([/w aɪ ˈ oʊ m ɪ ŋ/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/e/e9/En-us-Wyoming.ogg/En-us-Wyoming.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:En-us-Wyoming.ogg "File:En-us-Wyoming.ogg")[_wy-OH-ming_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"))[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-9) is a landlocked [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") in the [Mountain West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_states "Mountain states") subregion of the [Western United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States"). It borders [Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana "Montana") to the north and northwest, [South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dakota "South Dakota") and [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska") to the east, [Idaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho "Idaho") to the west, [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah") to the southwest, and [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") to the south. With an estimated population of 587,618 as of 2024,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-auto-7) Wyoming is the [least populous state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population "List of U.S. states and territories by population") despite being the [tenth-largest by area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories by area"), and it has the [second-lowest population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_by_population_density "List of U.S. states by population density"). The [state capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_capitals_in_the_United_States "List of capitals in the United States") and [most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_municipalities_in_Wyoming "List of municipalities in Wyoming") is [Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne,_Wyoming "Cheyenne, Wyoming").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-QF-10)

Wyoming's western half consists mostly of the ranges and rangelands of the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains"); its eastern half consists of high-elevation [prairie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prairie "Prairie"), and is referred to as the [High Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Plains_(United_States) "High Plains (United States)"). Wyoming's climate is [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") in some parts and [continental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_climate "Continental climate") in others, making it drier and windier overall than other states, with greater temperature extremes. The [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States") owns just under half of Wyoming's land; the state ranks sixth in the amount of land—and fifth in the proportion of its land—that is owned by the federal government.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-maineenvironment.org-11) Its federal lands include two national parks ([Grand Teton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Teton_National_Park "Grand Teton National Park") and [Yellowstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone_National_Park "Yellowstone National Park")), two national recreation areas, two national monuments, and several national forests, as well as historic sites, fish hatcheries, and wildlife refuges.

[Indigenous peoples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples "Indigenous peoples") have inhabited the region for thousands of years. Part of the land that became Wyoming came under American sovereignty via the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase"), part via the [Oregon Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Treaty "Oregon Treaty"), and, lastly, via the [Mexican Cession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Cession "Mexican Cession"). With the opening of the [Oregon Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Trail "Oregon Trail"), the [Mormon Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mormon_Trail "Mormon Trail"), and the [California Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California_Trail "California Trail"), vast numbers of pioneers traveled through parts of the state that had once been traversed mainly by fur trappers, and this spurred the establishment of forts, such as [Fort Laramie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Laramie_National_Historic_Site "Fort Laramie National Historic Site"), that today serve as population centers.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-12) The [Transcontinental Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_transcontinental_railroad "First transcontinental railroad") supplanted the wagon trails in 1867 with a route through southern Wyoming,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-13) bringing new settlers and the establishment of founding towns, including the state capital of Cheyenne.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-14) On July 10, 1890, Wyoming became the union's 44th state.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-WyoFacts-1)

[Women's suffrage in Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_suffrage_in_Wyoming "Women's suffrage in Wyoming") dates to 1869 when it granted women the right to vote as a territory, and in 1890 it became the first state allowing its woman citizens to vote. It also became the first state to allow women to hold elected office and the first to elect a female governor, [Nellie Tayloe Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellie_Tayloe_Ross "Nellie Tayloe Ross"). In honor of this part of its history, its official nickname is "The Equality State" and its official state motto is "Equal Rights".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-WyoFacts-1) Farming and ranching, and the attendant [range wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_war "Range war"), feature prominently in the state's history. Wyoming's economy is largely based on tourism and the extraction of minerals such as [coal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal "Coal"), [natural gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas "Natural gas"), [oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum "Petroleum"), and [trona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trona "Trona"). Its agricultural commodities include barley, hay, livestock, [sugar beets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sugar_beet "Sugar beet"), wheat, and wool.

## Etymology

The name _Wyoming_ originally denoted a [valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming_Valley "Wyoming Valley") in [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). It was made famous by [Thomas Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Campbell_(poet) "Thomas Campbell (poet)")'s poem "[Gertrude of Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gertrude_of_Wyoming "Gertrude of Wyoming")" (1808), which dramatizes the [Wyoming Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming_Massacre "Wyoming Massacre") of 1778. As a name for the region that would become the state of Wyoming, it was put forward by Representative [James Mitchell Ashley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Mitchell_Ashley "James Mitchell Ashley") of [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio") in 1865. Ashley argued that the name was both "beautiful" and semantically fitting for a region on the edge of the [Great Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains"), since it means "at the big plains" in the [Munsee Delaware language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munsee_language "Munsee language").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-15) When in 1868 a bill was introduced to organize this region as a [territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming_Territory "Wyoming Territory"), Congress considered the name _Lincoln_, but ultimately accepted Ashley's suggestion.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-State_of_Wyoming%E2%80%94Narrative-17)

## History

Main article: [History of Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Wyoming "History of Wyoming")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/08/Alfred_Jacob_Miller_-_Fort_Laramie_-_Walters_37194049.jpg/330px-Alfred_Jacob_Miller_-_Fort_Laramie_-_Walters_37194049.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alfred_Jacob_Miller_-_Fort_Laramie_-_Walters_37194049.jpg)

The first [Fort Laramie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Laramie "Fort Laramie") as it looked before 1840 (painting from memory by Alfred Jacob Miller)

Several [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") groups originally inhabited the region today known as Wyoming. The [Crow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crow_Nation "Crow Nation"), [Arapaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arapaho "Arapaho"), [Lakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakota_people "Lakota people"), and [Shoshone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoshone "Shoshone") were but a few of the original inhabitants European explorers encountered when they first visited the region. What is now southwestern Wyoming was claimed by the [Spanish Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire "Spanish Empire"), which extended through the Southwest and Mexico. With Mexican independence in 1821, it was considered part of [Alta California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alta_California "Alta California"). U.S. expansion brought settlers who fought for control. Mexico ceded these territories after its defeat in 1848 in the [Mexican–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican%E2%80%93American_War "Mexican–American War").

From the late 18th century, [French-Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French-Canadian "French-Canadian") trappers from Québec and Montréal regularly entered the area for trade with the tribes. French toponyms such as Téton and [La Ramie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_La_Ramee "Jacques La Ramee") are marks of that history.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-:1-18)

American [John Colter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Colter "John Colter") first recorded a description in English of the region in 1807. He was a member of the [Lewis and Clark Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition "Lewis and Clark Expedition"), which was guided by French Canadian [Toussaint Charbonneau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toussaint_Charbonneau "Toussaint Charbonneau") and his young Shoshone wife, [Sacagawea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacagawea "Sacagawea"). At the time, Colter's reports of the [Yellowstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Yellowstone_Ecosystem "Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem") area were considered fictional.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-19) On a return from [Astoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astoria,_Oregon "Astoria, Oregon"), [Robert Stuart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Stuart_(explorer) "Robert Stuart (explorer)") and a party of five men discovered [South Pass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pass_(Wyoming) "South Pass (Wyoming)") in 1812.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-:1-18)

The [Oregon Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Trail "Oregon Trail") later followed that route as emigrants moved to the west coast. In 1850, mountain man [Jim Bridger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Bridger "Jim Bridger") first documented what is now known as [Bridger Pass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridger_Pass "Bridger Pass").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-:2-20) Bridger also explored Yellowstone, and filed reports on the region that, like Colter's, were largely regarded at the time as [tall tales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tall_tale "Tall tale"). The [Union Pacific Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Pacific_Railroad "Union Pacific Railroad") constructed track through Bridger Pass in 1868.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-:2-20) It was used as the route for construction of [Interstate 80](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_80_in_Wyoming "Interstate 80 in Wyoming") through the mountains 90 years later.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-21)

After the Union Pacific Railroad reached [Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne,_Wyoming "Cheyenne, Wyoming") in 1867, population growth was stimulated. The federal government established the [Wyoming Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming_Territory "Wyoming Territory") on July 25, 1868.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-22) Lacking significant deposits of gold and silver, unlike mineral-rich [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), Wyoming did not have such a population boom. But [South Pass City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pass_City,_Wyoming "South Pass City, Wyoming") had a short-lived boom after the Carissa Mine began producing gold in 1867.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-23) Copper was mined in some areas between the [Sierra Madre Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Madre_Range_(Wyoming) "Sierra Madre Range (Wyoming)") and the Snowy Range near [Grand Encampment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Encampment,_Wyoming "Grand Encampment, Wyoming").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-24)

Once government-sponsored expeditions to the Yellowstone country began, Colter's and Bridger's descriptions of the region's landscape were confirmed. In 1872, [Yellowstone National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone_National_Park "Yellowstone National Park") was created as the world's first, to protect this area. Nearly all of the park lies within the northwestern corner of Wyoming.

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7a/3c_Wyoming_Statehood_50th_anniversary%2C_1940_issue.jpg/250px-3c_Wyoming_Statehood_50th_anniversary%2C_1940_issue.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:3c_Wyoming_Statehood_50th_anniversary,_1940_issue.jpg)

On July 10, 1940, the U.S. Post Office issued a postage stamp commemorating the 50th anniversary of Wyoming statehood. The engraving depicts the Wyoming state seal, which features a central figure of a woman in front of a banner reading 'equal rights'

On December 10, 1869, territorial Governor [John Allen Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Allen_Campbell "John Allen Campbell") extended the right to vote to women, making Wyoming the first territory to do so, and upon statehood became the first state to grant [women's suffrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Women's_suffrage "Women's suffrage").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-25) Women first served on juries in Wyoming ([Laramie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laramie,_Wyoming "Laramie, Wyoming") in 1870). Wyoming was also a pioneer in welcoming women into electoral politics.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-Helton-26) It had the first female court bailiff (Mary Atkinson, Laramie, in 1870), and the first female [justice of the peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justice_of_the_peace "Justice of the peace") in the country ([Esther Hobart Morris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esther_Hobart_Morris "Esther Hobart Morris"), South Pass City, in 1870). In 1924, Wyoming was the first state to elect a female governor, [Nellie Tayloe Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nellie_Tayloe_Ross "Nellie Tayloe Ross"), who took office in January 1925.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-27) Due to its civil-rights history, one of Wyoming's state nicknames is "The Equality State", and the official state motto is "Equal Rights".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-WyoFacts-1)

Wyoming's constitution also included a pioneering article on [water rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_right "Water right").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-28) Bills for Wyoming Territory's admission to the union were introduced in both the [U.S. Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") and [U.S. House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") in December 1889. On March 27, 1890, the House passed the bill and President [Benjamin Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Harrison "Benjamin Harrison") signed Wyoming's statehood bill; Wyoming became the 44th state in the union on July 10, 1890.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-WyoFacts-1)

Wyoming was the location of the [Johnson County War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnson_County_War "Johnson County War") of 1892, which erupted between competing groups of cattle ranchers. The passage of the [Homestead Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Act "Homestead Act") led to an influx of small ranchers. A [range war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Range_war "Range war") broke out when either or both of the groups chose violent conflict over commercial competition in the use of the public land.

## Geography

Main article: [Geography of Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geography_of_Wyoming "Geography of Wyoming")

### Climate

Further information: [Climate change in Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change_in_Wyoming "Climate change in Wyoming")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/K%C3%B6ppen_Climate_Types_Wyoming.png/250px-K%C3%B6ppen_Climate_Types_Wyoming.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:K%C3%B6ppen_Climate_Types_Wyoming.png)

[Köppen climate types](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") of Wyoming, using 1991–2020 [climate normals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climatological_normal "Climatological normal")

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Autumn_in_the_Bighorn_Mountains.JPG/250px-Autumn_in_the_Bighorn_Mountains.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Autumn_in_the_Bighorn_Mountains.JPG)

Autumn in the Bighorn Mountains

Wyoming's climate is generally [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") and [continental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_climate "Continental climate") ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification")_[\_BSk\_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold\_steppe "Cold steppe")_) and is drier and windier in comparison to most of the United States with greater temperature extremes.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-29)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-30) Much of this is due to the topography of the state. Summers in Wyoming are warm with July high temperatures averaging between 80 and 90°F (27 and 32°C) in most of the state. With increasing elevation, however, this average drops rapidly with locations above 9,000 feet (2,700 m) averaging around 70°F (21°C). Summer nights throughout the state are characterized by a rapid cooldown with even the hottest locations averaging in the 50–60°F (10–16°C) range at night. In most of the state, most of the precipitation tends to fall in the late spring and early summer. Winters are cold but are variable with periods of sometimes extreme cold interspersed between generally mild periods, with [Chinook winds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinook_winds "Chinook winds") providing unusually warm temperatures in some locations.

Wyoming is a dry state with much of the land receiving less than 10 inches (250 mm) of rainfall per year. Precipitation depends on elevation with lower areas in the [Big Horn Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bighorn_Basin "Bighorn Basin") averaging 5–8 inches (130–200 mm), making the area nearly a true [desert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desert "Desert"). The lower areas in the North and on the eastern plains typically average around 10–12 inches (250–300 mm), making the climate there [semi-arid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid "Semi-arid"). Some mountain areas do receive a good amount of precipitation, 20 inches (510 mm) or more, much of it as snow, sometimes 200 inches (510 cm) or more annually. The state's highest recorded temperature is 114°F (46°C) at [Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basin,_Wyoming "Basin, Wyoming") on July 12, 1900, and the lowest recorded temperature is −66°F (−54°C) at [Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside,_Wyoming "Riverside, Wyoming") on February 9, 1933.

The number of [thunderstorm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorm "Thunderstorm") days varies across the state with the southeastern plains of the state having the most days of thunderstorm activity. Thunderstorm activity in the state is highest during the late spring and early summer. The southeastern corner of the state is the most vulnerable part of the state to [tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado") activity. Moving away from that point and westwards, the incidence of tornadoes drops dramatically with the west part of the state showing little vulnerability. Tornadoes, where they occur, tend to be small and brief, unlike some of those that occur farther east.

### Location and size

As specified in the designating legislation for the [Territory of Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territory_of_Wyoming "Territory of Wyoming"), Wyoming's borders are lines of [latitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latitude "Latitude")[41°N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/41st_parallel_north "41st parallel north") and [45°N](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/45th_parallel_north "45th parallel north"), and [longitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longitude "Longitude") 104°3'W and 111°3'W (27 and 34 west of the [Washington Meridian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Meridian "Washington Meridian")) – a [geodesic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geodesic "Geodesic") quadrangle.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-36) Wyoming is one of only three states (the others being [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado") and [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah")) to have borders defined by _only_ "straight" lines. Due to surveying inaccuracies during the 19th century, Wyoming's legal border deviates from the true [latitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latitude "Latitude") and [longitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longitude "Longitude") lines by up to one-half mile (0.80 km) in some spots, especially in the mountainous region along the [45th parallel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/45th_parallel_north "45th parallel north").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-37) Wyoming is bordered on the north by [Montana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana "Montana"), on the east by [South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dakota "South Dakota") and [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska"), on the south by [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), on the southwest by [Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utah "Utah"), and on the west by [Idaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho "Idaho"). It is the tenth largest state in the United States in total area, containing 97,814 square miles (253,340 km 2) and is made up of 23 counties. From the north border to the south border, it is 276 miles (444 km); and from the east to the west border is 365 miles (587 km) at its south end and 342 miles (550 km) at the north end.

### Natural landforms

#### Mountain ranges

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Barns_grand_tetons.jpg/250px-Barns_grand_tetons.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Barns_grand_tetons.jpg)

[Teton Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teton_Range "Teton Range")

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Cattle_Drive_near_Pinedale%2C_WY_%2814963962303%29.jpg/250px-Cattle_Drive_near_Pinedale%2C_WY_%2814963962303%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cattle_Drive_near_Pinedale,_WY_(14963962303).jpg)

[Green River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_River_(Colorado_River_tributary) "Green River (Colorado River tributary)") valley

The [Great Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") meet the [Rocky Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") in Wyoming. The state is a great [plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plateau "Plateau") broken by many [mountain ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_range "Mountain range"). Surface elevations range from the summit of [Gannett Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gannett_Peak "Gannett Peak") in the [Wind River Mountain Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_River_Range "Wind River Range"), at 13,804 feet (4,207 m), to the [Belle Fourche River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belle_Fourche_River "Belle Fourche River") valley in the state's northeast corner, at 3,125 feet (952 m). In the northwest are the [Absaroka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absaroka_Range "Absaroka Range"), [Owl Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owl_Creek_Mountains "Owl Creek Mountains"), [Gros Ventre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gros_Ventre_Range "Gros Ventre Range"), [Wind River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_River_Range "Wind River Range"), and the [Teton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teton_Range "Teton Range") ranges. In the north central are the [Big Horn Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Horn_Mountains "Big Horn Mountains"); in the northeast, the [Black Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Hills "Black Hills"); and in the southern region the [Laramie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laramie_Mountains "Laramie Mountains"), [Snowy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine_Bow_Mountains "Medicine Bow Mountains"), and [Sierra Madre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Madre_Range_(Wyoming) "Sierra Madre Range (Wyoming)") ranges.

The Snowy Range in the south-central part of the state is an extension of the Colorado [Rockies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Mountains "Rocky Mountains") both in geology and in appearance. The Wind River Range in the west central part of the state is remote and includes more than 40 mountain peaks in excess of 13,000 ft (4,000 m) tall in addition to [Gannett Peak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gannett_Peak "Gannett Peak"), the highest peak in the state. The Bighorn Mountains in the north-central portion are somewhat isolated from the bulk of the Rocky Mountains.

The Teton Range in the northwest extends for 50 miles (80 km), part of which is included in [Grand Teton National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Teton_National_Park "Grand Teton National Park"). The park includes the [Grand Teton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Teton "Grand Teton"), the second-highest peak in the state.

The [Continental Divide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continental_Divide "Continental Divide") spans north–south across the central portion of the state. Rivers east of the divide drain into the [Missouri River Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River_Basin "Missouri River Basin") and eventually the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"). They are the [North Platte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Platte_River "North Platte River"), [Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_River_(Wyoming) "Wind River (Wyoming)"), [Bighorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bighorn_River "Bighorn River"), and [Yellowstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone_River "Yellowstone River") rivers. The [Snake River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_River "Snake River") in northwest Wyoming eventually drains into the [Columbia River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_River "Columbia River") and the Pacific Ocean, as does the [Green River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_River_(Colorado_River) "Green River (Colorado River)") through the [Colorado River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_River "Colorado River") Basin.

The Continental Divide forks in the south-central part of the state in an area known as the [Great Divide Basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Divide_Basin "Great Divide Basin") where water that precipitates onto or flows into it cannot reach an ocean—it _all_ sinks into the soil and eventually evaporates.

Several rivers begin in or flow through the state, including the Yellowstone River, Bighorn River, Green River, and the Snake River.

#### Basins

Much of Wyoming is covered with large basins containing different eco-regions, from shrublands to smaller patches of desert.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-Wyo-basins-38) Regions of the state classified as basins contain everything from large geologic formations to sand dunes and vast unpopulated spaces.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-Ecoregions-Wyoming-39) Basin landscapes are typically at lower elevations and include rolling hills, valleys, mesas, terraces and other rugged terrain, but also include natural springs as well as rivers and artificial reservoirs.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-epaEcoregionsofWyoming-40) They have common plant species such as various subspecies of [sagebrush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artemisia_tridentata "Artemisia tridentata"), [juniper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juniper "Juniper") and grasses such as [wheatgrass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agropyron "Agropyron"), but basins are known for their diversity of plant and animal species.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-Wyo-basins-38)

#### Islands

For a more comprehensive list, see [List of islands of Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Wyoming "List of islands of Wyoming").

Wyoming has 32 named islands; the majority are in [Jackson Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Lake_(Wyoming) "Jackson Lake (Wyoming)") and [Yellowstone Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone_Lake "Yellowstone Lake"), within [Yellowstone National Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellowstone_National_Park "Yellowstone National Park") in the northwest portion of the state. The [Green River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_River_(Colorado_River) "Green River (Colorado River)") in the southwest also contains a number of islands.

### Population

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9a/Wyoming_population_density_2020.png/500px-Wyoming_population_density_2020.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wyoming_population_density_2020.png)

The largest population centers are [Cheyenne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheyenne,_WY_MSA "Cheyenne, WY MSA") (southeast) and [Casper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casper,_WY,_MSA "Casper, WY, MSA").

The [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census") counted 576,851 people living in Wyoming.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-:3-46) The [center of population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_of_population "Center of population") of Wyoming is in [Natrona County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natrona_County,_Wyoming "Natrona County, Wyoming").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-47)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-48) Sparsely populated, Wyoming is the least populous state of the United States. Wyoming has the second-lowest population density in the country (behind [Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska "Alaska")) and is the sparsest-populated of the 48 [contiguous states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contiguous_states "Contiguous states"). It is one of only two states with a population smaller than that of the nation's capital; the only other state with this distinction is [Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont "Vermont").

According to [HUD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Housing_and_Urban_Development "United States Department of Housing and Urban Development")'s 2022 [Annual Homeless Assessment Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annual_Homeless_Assessment_Report_to_Congress "Annual Homeless Assessment Report to Congress"), there were an estimated 648 [homeless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homelessness "Homelessness") people in Wyoming.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-49)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-50)

According to the 2020 census, the population's racial composition was 84.7% [white](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_American "White American") (81.4% non-Hispanic white), 2.4% American Indian and Alaska Native, 0.9% Black or African American, 0.9% Asian American, and 0.1% Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, 3.5% from some other race, and 7.5% from two or more races.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-2020DP1-51) As of 2011, 24.9% of Wyoming's population younger than age 1 were minorities.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-52) According to data from the [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey"), as of 2018, Wyoming was the only U.S. state where African Americans earn a higher median income than white workers.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-53)

As of 2015, Wyoming had an estimated population of 586,107, which was an increase of 1,954, or 0.29%, from the prior year and an increase of 22,481, or 3.99%, since the [2010 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_Census "2010 United States Census"). This includes a natural increase since the last census of 12,165 (33,704 births minus 21,539 deaths) and an increase from net migration of 4,035 into the state. Immigration resulted in a net increase of 2,264 and migration within the country produced a net increase of 1,771. In 2004, the foreign-born population was 11,000 (2.2%). In 2005, total births in Wyoming were 7,231 (birth rate of 14.04 per thousand).[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-54)

Wyoming experienced its first population decline since 1990, with a decrease of just over 1,000 people (0.2 percent) from July 2015 to July 2016. This decline was attributed to the downturn in the state's mineral extraction industry, particularly the oil and gas sector, which led to the loss of thousands of jobs. However, state economist Jim Robinson noted signs of economic stabilization. Job losses in the oil and gas industry appeared to have leveled off, and there was a slight increase in drilling activity in recent months. While the state's economy showed little growth, it was considered to have reached a more stable condition as of late 2016.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-55)

According to the 2000 census, the largest ancestry groups in Wyoming were: [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German-American "German-American") (25.9%), [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_American "English American") (15.9%), [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_American "Irish American") (13.3%), and [American Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") (4.7%). An additional 6.4% responded with "American" as their ancestry.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-56)

In 2018, the top countries of origin for Wyoming's immigrants were [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England") and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-57)

### Languages

See also: [Native American languages of Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_languages_of_Wyoming "Native American languages of Wyoming")

In 2010, 93.39% (474,343) of Wyomingites over age 5 spoke [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") as their [primary language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_language "Primary language"); 4.47% (22,722) spoke [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"), 0.35% (1,771) spoke [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language "German language"), and 0.28% (1,434) spoke [French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"). Other common non-English languages included [Algonquian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquian_languages "Algonquian languages") (0.18%), [Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language") (0.10%), [Tagalog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagalog_language "Tagalog language"), and [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language "Greek language") (both 0.09%).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-69)

In 2007, the [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey") reported 6.2% (30,419) of Wyoming's population over five spoke a language other than English at home. Of those, 68.1% were able to speak English very well, 16.0% spoke English well, 10.9% did not speak English well, and 5.0% did not speak English at all.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-Language2007-70)

In 2020, the [Public Religion Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Religion_Research_Institute "Public Religion Research Institute") determined that about 55% of Wyoming's adult population was [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity"), primarily [evangelical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelicalism "Evangelicalism") and [mainline Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainline_Protestant "Mainline Protestant"), [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church"), and [Mormon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mormonism "Mormonism"). The Public Religion Research Institute survey documented a decrease in religiosity from a 2014 separate [Pew Research Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Research_Center "Pew Research Center") study;[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-pew2014-72) according to the Public Religion Research Institute, the unaffiliated made up 40% of the state population by 2020. According to a 2013 Gallup poll, Wyomingites' religious affiliations were 49% Protestant, 23% [nonreligious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonreligious "Nonreligious") or other, 18% Catholic, 9% [Latter-day Saint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latter_Day_Saint_movement "Latter Day Saint movement") (Mormons), and less than 1% [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaism "Judaism").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-73)

A 2010 [Association of Religion Data Archives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_Religion_Data_Archives "Association of Religion Data Archives") (ARDA) report recognized as Wyoming's largest denominations [the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Church_of_Jesus_Christ_of_Latter-day_Saints "The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints") (LDS Church), with 62,804 (11%); the Catholic Church, with 61,222 (10.8%); and the [Southern Baptist Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Baptist_Convention "Southern Baptist Convention"), with 15,812 (2.8%). The report counted 59,247 evangelical Protestants (10.5%), 36,539 mainline Protestants (6.5%), 785 Eastern Orthodox Christians; 281 Black Protestants; 65,000 adhering to other traditions; and 340,552 claiming no religious tradition.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-74) In 2020, ARDA reported the state's largest individual denominations as the following: the Catholic Church (69,500); the LDS Church (67,729); and the Southern Baptist Convention (11,082). Non-denominational Protestants were 23,410 in number.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming#cite_note-75)
